editorial:
When a father passes away, four grown siblings are forced back into their childhood home for a full week of sitting shiva. You'll meet Jason Bateman's Judd, who just caught his wife cheating, Tina Fey's Wendy, who is juggling her own messy life, Adam Driver's Phillip, the wild youngest brother, and Corey Stoll's Paul, the responsible eldest. Their free-speaking mother, played by Jane Fonda, adds fuel to the fire. The house becomes a pressure cooker of old grudges, buried secrets, and awkward family dinners. The vibe is warm but chaotic, like a holiday gathering that never ends. You feel the love underneath all the yelling, and the humor lands in those small, relatable moments that only family can create.

The acting is the real draw here. Every cast member brings heart and comic timing, especially Bateman and Fey, who make you believe they have decades of shared history. The pacing moves quickly, jumping between subplots without losing steam. On the downside, some storylines feel rushed and the ending wraps up a little too neatly. Still, if you enjoy family dramedies with big laughs and real emotion, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Judd finally confronts his feelings about his failed marriage and decides to move forward instead of looking back. The siblings share a quiet moment together, realizing that despite all their fights, they still need each other. Their mother reveals she has been hiding her own struggles but is ready to face them. The family gathers one last time before leaving the house, choosing to stay connected rather than drift apart. It ends on a hopeful note, showing that healing takes time but love holds them together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramedies with big laughs and real emotion.
